transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Thanks for seeing me. Man, I just... I don't really know where to start, but I guess I'm here because things have been getting really out of hand lately with how I eat. I'm a diesel mechanic, right? I work on these massive buses and commercial trucks, and the shifts are just brutal. I mean, you're on your feet all day, wrestling with heavy parts, covered in grease, and by the time I finally clock out, I'm just completely wiped. 

But lately, when I get off one of those long shifts—or even if I'm just up late trying to study some new engine schematics—I end up eating just... way, way more than I ever planned to. I'll stop on the way home and get a massive fast-food meal, like a couple of burgers, large fries, maybe a shake. But then I get home and it's like a switch flips. I'll eat all of that, and then I'll just keep going. I'll rip into whatever snacks I have in the pantry, grab a whole bag of chips, and then I'm just standing there with the fridge wide open, eating whatever's inside. Leftovers, random slices of cheese, just anything I can get my hands on. And it's all in one sitting. It's like I completely lose track of what I'm doing until I've eaten half the kitchen, and I just can't seem to stop doing it.
After these episodes of eating a lot, do you ever try to make up for it by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or doing something else to try to control your weight or how much you’ve eaten?

Yeah... man, it’s honestly pretty tough to talk about, but... yeah, I do. It’s just, after I eat all that stuff—like I was saying, the burgers and the chips and whatever else I can find—my stomach just gets so painfully full. It feels like I swallowed a cinder block. And I just sit there on the couch, or sometimes I'm still standing right there in the kitchen, and this massive wave of panic just hits me. I start thinking about all that grease and sugar just sitting in my gut, and I get so scared of what all that food is going to do to me. 

I mean, my job is really physical, right? I have to squeeze under axles and maneuver around these massive engine blocks, and I just get terrified that I'm gonna blow up like a balloon and not even be able to do my job right, or just ruin my body completely. So... yeah, a lot of times, I’ll go straight into the bathroom. I usually turn on the exhaust fan and run the sink so it’s loud just in case, and I’ll make myself throw up. Just to get it out. To feel empty again, or at least undo the damage. 

And then, if I can’t do that, or if I feel like I didn't get it all out, I’ll use laxatives. I started keeping a box of them in my bathroom cabinet, actually bought them at the pharmacy right down the street from the shop. At first, it was just every once in a while, but then I started taking them more because the fear of the food just staying in my system completely freaks me out. I just have to get rid of it, you know? Even if it means I feel like absolute garbage the next morning at work, sweating and running to the bathroom, I just can't stand the thought of all that food staying inside me. It's like I have to hit a reset button no matter what it takes.

Can you describe what it feels like right before one of these eating episodes? Do you feel like you can't control how much you're going to eat once you start, or does it feel more like you're making a choice to eat a lot?

Well, right before... it's weird, man. It usually starts when I'm walking out of the bay at the shop. I'm standing there at the sink, scrubbing the grease off my hands with that heavy-duty orange pumice soap, you know? And my brain is just completely fried. I'm so exhausted, my back is aching from being hunched under a chassis all day, and I'll tell myself, "Okay, I'm just gonna go straight home, maybe make a normal turkey sandwich, take a hot shower, and just crash." That's the plan. That's always the plan when I clock out. 

But then I get in my truck, and I start driving, and the closer I get to home, it's like my brain just gets hijacked. I'll see the neon sign for the drive-thru, and I think, "Okay, maybe just one combo meal. Just to take the edge off because I'm starving and I worked a twelve-hour shift." So I pull in. I order. I tell myself it's just gonna be that one meal. But by the time I get home and sit down with it... man, it is definitely not a choice anymore. Not even a little bit. 

Once I start on those nights, it feels like my hands just keep grabbing food, like they have a completely separate mind of their own. I'll finish the fast food, and then I'm up and pacing around the kitchen. I'll be tearing into a bag of Doritos, or grabbing handfuls of cereal, just whatever is there. And the craziest, scariest part is that inside my head, I'm literally screaming at myself. I’m telling myself to stop. I'm thinking, "What are you doing? Just put the bag down, you're ruining everything." I'll be doing it even while I’m already feeling sick to my stomach. My gut will be stretching, it actually physically hurts, and I know I'm gonna have to deal with the panic afterward, but I just can't stop. 

It's like I'm a passenger in my own body, just watching some other guy shovel food into my mouth. I'll be chewing and swallowing, feeling absolutely miserable, but my hands just won't stop reaching for the next thing. I have absolutely zero power to hit the brakes once that switch flips. It's just this frantic, desperate feeling until there's literally nothing left in front of me to eat. So, yeah... it's definitely not a choice. It feels like the exact opposite of a choice.
